diagnostic_steps.action: Parse log stream for OOMKilled events
findings: Detected 5+ OOMKilled events across payment-processor pods
Exit code 137 confirmed for all killed containers

diagnostic_steps.action: Correlate memory metrics with OOM events
findings: Memory usage spiked from 7.5GB to 8.3GB before first OOM
Node memory available dropped to 4GB after OOM events
Pod restart rate: 5 restarts for payment-processor-7f8b9-k2x4m
CPU usage at 98.5% indicates memory pressure causing CPU thrashing

diagnostic_steps.action: Map service dependencies and resource allocation
findings: All pods share same node pool: aks-worker-01, -02, -03

diagnostic_steps.action: Identify root cause using combined evidence
findings: Root cause: Payment transaction spike caused memory exhaustion
Memory limits too low for peak load (8GB insufficient)
Cascading failure: Redis OOM caused payment-processor to fallback to direct connections, increasing memory usage
Node memory pressure triggered eviction chain
diagnostic_steps.root_cause: Insufficient memory limits combined with unexpected traffic spike

recommendations.command: kubectl set resources deployment payment-processor --limits=memory=12Gi --requests=memory=8Gi -n payment-service
recommendations.rationale: Increase memory limit to handle peak loads with 50% headroom

recommendations.command: kubectl set resources deployment redis-cache --limits=memory=6Gi --requests=memory=4Gi -n payment-service
recommendations.rationale: Increase Redis memory to prevent OOM during cache pressure
Enable HPA to scale horizontally under load

recommendations.command:
kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: payment-processor-pdb
  namespace: payment-service
spec:
  minAvailable: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-processor
EOF
recommendations.rationale: Ensure minimum replicas during scaling events

remediation_validation: Monitor memory usage for 30 minutes after remediation
Verify no OOMKilled events in logs
